renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: partner_chords
  title: Fusion partner map
  description: |-
    Each chord joins the two breakpoints of a fusion on the genome, with its width the read support and its colour the event class. It answers where in the genome the partners sit and how strongly each fusion is supported.
    How to read: chords within one chromosome arc are local events such as deletions and duplications, and chords between chromosomes are translocations. A thick chord is a well supported fusion, so hover it for its partner genes.
    Lines and annotations: chord width is the split reads on both sides plus the discordant mates, as defined by the recipe, and the event class is Arriba's own type.
  kind: genome_chord
  roles:
    chrom_a: chrom_a
    pos_a: pos_a
    chrom_b: chrom_b
    pos_b: pos_b
    label: label
    weight: weight
    category: category

- component: figure
  id: class_by_confidence
  title: Support by event type and confidence
  description: |-
    Each bar stacks the fusions of one event type, with height their supporting reads and colour Arriba's confidence class. It answers which kinds of event are well supported.
    How to read: tall high-confidence segments mark reliable events. Low-confidence segments are the calls Arriba's authors advise treating with skepticism.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33441414/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: category
    y: weight
    color: confidence
    labels:
      category: Event type
      weight: Supporting reads
      confidence: Confidence

- component: card
  title: Link weight
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median read support of a fusion link, the split reads on both sides plus the discordant mates, with the lowest and highest beside it. It answers how thick a typical chord is.
    How to read: a low median means the map is made of weakly supported links. The range is wide, so a box would draw a flat line.
  column: weight
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: median, lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: Fusions by event type
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct fusions drawn, and the bars rank the event types by how many they hold. It answers which kind of rearrangement dominates.
    How to read: translocations and deletions point to different mechanisms, and a run with mostly read-through events may reflect transcription between neighbours and not a true fusion.
  column: label
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: category
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fusions, by event type

- component: card
  title: Event type composition
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of links and the ring splits them by event type. It answers what share of links each kind of event holds.
    How to read: a ring with one dominant slice means one mechanism accounts for most of the calls. The second number is how many event types are present.
  column: category
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: category
  caption: links, by event type

- component: interactive
  title: Confidence filter
  description: |-
    Pick one or more of Arriba's confidence classes to restrict the tiles of this tab to them. It answers what the map looks like when only the reliable calls are kept.
    How to read: choose high, or high and medium, to drop the low-confidence calls that Arriba's authors advise treating with skepticism.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33441414/
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: confidence

- component: table
  title: Breakpoint links table
  description: |-
    Each row is a fusion link with its two breakpoint loci, its read support, its event type and its confidence. It answers the exact coordinates behind each chord and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by weight to find the best supported links.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: label

- component: advanced_viz
  id: evidence_dot_plot
  title: Evidence for each fusion
  description: |-
    Each dot is a fusion in one confidence class: its colour is the read support on a log scale and its size is the share of local reads that support it. It answers which calls rest on strong evidence and how confident Arriba is in them.
    How to read: a large, dark dot in the high-confidence column is a well supported call. A call with few supporting reads in the low-confidence column is weak and Arriba's authors advise treating such calls with skepticism unless other evidence corroborates them. Check the table for the breakpoints and domains of the calls you keep.
    Lines and annotations: the colour scale is log10 of supporting reads plus 1, a transform of this catalog's recipe, where supporting reads are the split reads plus the discordant mates Arriba reports. The confidence classes low, medium and high are assigned by Arriba.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33441414/
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: confidence
    gene: fusion
    mean_expression: log_support
    frac_expressing: support_fraction

- component: advanced_viz
  id: partner_chrom_sankey
  title: Partner chromosomes
  description: |-
    Each flow joins the chromosome of the 5' partner on the left to the chromosome of the 3' partner on the right, with its width the number of fusions. It answers whether the fusions are within one chromosome or between chromosomes.
    How to read: a flow that returns to the same chromosome is a local rearrangement such as a deletion, an inversion or a duplication. A flow to another chromosome is a translocation. Many flows from one chromosome may point to a hot region or to a recurrent artefact worth checking.
  kind: sankey
  config:
    value_label: Fusions
  roles:
    steps:
    - chrom_5p
    - chrom_3p

- component: figure
  id: type_bars
  title: Support by event type
  description: |-
    Each bar stacks the calls of one event type, such as a deletion, a duplication or a translocation, with height the supporting reads and colour the confidence class. It answers which kinds of event carry the evidence.
    How to read: tall bars in the high-confidence colour are well supported events. An event type made only of low-confidence calls is mostly noise, so filter it out before interpreting the run.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33441414/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fusion_type
    y: supporting_reads
    color: confidence
    labels:
      fusion_type: Event type
      supporting_reads: Supporting reads
      confidence: Confidence

- component: figure
  id: site_bars
  title: Support by breakpoint location
  description: |-
    Each bar groups calls by the transcript feature the 5' breakpoint falls in, such as coding sequence, splice site or intron, with colour the feature of the 3' breakpoint and height the supporting reads. It answers whether breakpoints land where a spliced fusion transcript is expected.
    How to read: breakpoints at splice sites or in coding sequence on both sides are the usual shape of a real fusion. Calls with a breakpoint deep in an intron or in an untranslated region are less likely to produce a protein, so look at them with the reading frame tile.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: site_5p
    y: supporting_reads
    color: site_3p
    labels:
      site_5p: Transcript feature at the 5' breakpoint
      supporting_reads: Supporting reads
      site_3p: Transcript feature at the 3' breakpoint

- component: figure
  id: type_frame_bars
  title: Reading frame by event type
  description: |-
    Each bar stacks the calls of one event type, with height the supporting reads and colour whether the fusion keeps the reading frame. It answers which events are predicted to encode a protein.
    How to read: an in-frame fusion can produce a chimeric protein and is the first to follow up. An out-of-frame call is less likely to be functional, although the reading frame is one of several features used to judge a driver.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33441414/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fusion_type
    y: supporting_reads
    color: reading_frame
    labels:
      fusion_type: Event type
      supporting_reads: Supporting reads
      reading_frame: Reading frame

- component: card
  title: Supporting reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of supporting reads per call, the split reads plus the discordant mates, with the lowest and highest beside it. It answers how strong the evidence is for a typical call.
    How to read: a very low median means the calls rest on a handful of reads. The range is wide, so a box would draw a flat line.
  column: supporting_reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: median, lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: Fusions called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct fusions, and the bars rank the confidence classes by how many they hold. It answers how many fusions Arriba calls and how many it trusts.
    How to read: a run dominated by high and medium confidence is cleaner than one made of low-confidence calls, which Arriba's authors advise treating with skepticism.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33441414/
  column: fusion
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: confidence
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fusions, by confidence
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Split reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of split reads, reads that span the breakpoint, and the bars rank the event types by how many they carry. It answers where the direct junction evidence comes from.
    How to read: split reads show the exact breakpoint, whereas discordant mates only show the two partners are joined. A call with discordant mates only has an uncertain breakpoint.
  column: split_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: fusion_type
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: split reads, by event type

- component: card
  title: Share of local reads that support the fusion
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the reads around a breakpoint that support the fusion, between 0 and 1, and the histogram shows its distribution over the calls. It answers how dominant the fusion is over the normal transcript.
    How to read: a high share means most local reads carry the fusion, as in a clonal driver. A tiny share means a minor or artefactual signal.
  column: support_fraction
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution across calls

- component: table
  title: Fusion calls table
  description: |-
    Each row is a fusion call with its partners, breakpoints, event type, confidence, reading frame, read support and retained protein domains. It answers which fusions to validate and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by confidence and supporting reads, then check the reading frame and the retained domains of the kinase or other drivers of interest.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: fusion
